recipes.name: Chef John’s Homemade Chicken Noodle Soup
ingredients_raw: 2 quarts roasted chicken broth (see footnote for recipe link)
2 cooked boneless chicken breast halves, cubed
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Melt butter in a large soup pot over medium heat. Stir in carrot, onion, celery, thyme, and salt. Add chicken fat; cook and stir until onions turn soft and translucent, 5 to 6 minutes.
Stir in roasted chicken broth and bring to a boil. Season with salt, if necessary.
Stir in egg noodles; cook until tender, about 5 minutes.
Add cooked chicken breast meat; simmer until heated through, about 5 minutes. Season with cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper.

raw_recipe.headline: Chef John’s Homemade Chicken Noodle Soup
raw_recipe.description: This homemade chicken noodle soup is Chef John’s soul-warming and deliciously simple recipe that uses a flavorful homemade roasted chicken stock.

video.description: Welcome to Chef John's culinary haven, where he unveils his heartwarming Homemade Chicken Noodle Soup recipe! In this soul-soothing video, his expertise shines as he guides you through crafting this classic comfort dish from scratch. Watch the flavors dance together, from tender chicken and wholesome vegetables to slurp-worthy noodles, all simmered to perfection. Whether it's a rainy day or you need a cozy pick-me-up, this soup will warm your heart and soul. Get ready to savor every spoonful of this timeless, homemade delight!

review.reviewBody: I love how simple this recipe is. This is just plain comfort food. It all comes together so quickly too. I weighed the 4 oz of egg noodles and measured them - it was about 2 cups in my large glass pyrex measuring cup. Remember your soup will only be as good as your broth / stock. Enjoy!

Awesome!!! We love this soup, all I had was 2 quarts of regular chicken broth, but I went back to the store and bought one more quart of chicken stock because we like the extra liquid in our soup, the stock makes the difference. Perfect for a day you don't want to do alot of cooking. Thx

Changed a couple of things. Poached the chicken breasts with a little olive oil, celery and onion with chicken granules and four cups of water. Brought it to a boil and then turned off the stove; one hour later perfectly poached chicken. Shredded the chicken and sieved the ingredients from the broth. Used the chicken and the broth with some homemade amish egg noodles; plus all other ingredients. Did not have chicken fat so I used canola oil instead. This was absolutely delicious. I think my method is a lot easier with less work and the taste plus presentation is wonderful,

It's amazing that such a simple, easy recipe can be so good. It's my favorite chicken noodle soup anywhere.

As is, the recipe is fantastic. I've made this dozens of times, and here's my personal tips I've found that get the most of of it (at least for me).

1) Use a Costco (or supermarket) rotisserie chicken. It's already cooked and has the best flavor that the soup will really absorb. 

2) I once opted for a more expensive "Amish brand" style fat egg noodle, and the noodle was amazing. I never thought it would make such a big difference. Now I consider it mandatory when I make it :)

3) Fresh thyme is really important. I've tried with dried versions, and even freeze-dried, but still is best with fresh. 

4) I double the amount of each vegetable (carrot, celery, and onion) and use a bit more butter to compensate. Just a personal preference; it just seems to be a bit light on veggies if the regular amount is used. Either way its still great.

5) Always make more than you'll eat in one sitting as the next day the flavors are even better. 

Thanks Chef John - as always - great work.

Very nice soup! I made the Roasted Chicken Broth, omitting the tomato ketchup, and followed this recipe with 2 exceptions. I used leeks instead of onions, and I added 1/2 c. of dry white wine to the broth before adding the noodles and the chicken. Yum!

This is chicken soup as it should be - absolutely excellent. My family has been making this since I was a little girl- probably longer than that (without cayenne - we use Hungarian Paprika) Sometimes we put potato instead of noodles - depending on whether it is for dinner as a starter or supper with a baguette. Thanks for being such a`user friendly`chef, Chef John. Love your methods and your attitude.

I used this as the base recipe, but made some changes for what I call Scarborough Fair Chicken Soup.
I heated 3 quarts of Progresso Chicken Broth in a 6-qt stockpot. I sautéed the onion (3/4 cup), carrot (one cup) and celery (3/4 cup) in Avacado oil on medium-high heat and stirred in 2 tsp parsley, 1 tsp sage, 1 tsp rosemary and 1/2 tsp thyme, salt, pepper and red pepper to taste. When the onions were translucent, I added the contents of the skillet to the stockpot and slowly came to a boil. I de-boned a whole rotisserie chicken cut into small cubes and added it to the stockpot after about 30 minutes. I increases the heat to get the pot boiling and added the egg noodles. After 8 minutes, reduced heat and thickened a little with corn starch before serving. It is very bold and flavorful.

Excellent! Best chicken noodle soup I ever had. I made semi home made stock using a bought a rotisserie chicken and took the meat off of it, saving the meat to be used in the soup. Using the skin and bones, I added it to 3 cartons of store bought chicken broth. simmered for 3 hours with vegetables (carrots, celery, onion, peppercorn 2 bay leaves and thyme). strained it after 3 hours of simmering and cooled the stock for several hours. Then I followed the recipe exactly as written. It was excellent. This will be the chicken soup I'll make going forward.
Did not have time to make stock so used Swansons. Also used 3 cans chicken breast drained. Cooked noodles separate. Yum! Froze leftovers and even better second time.

The soup is great. I typically make a recipe as is & do my critique. Then the next time I make it, (if I like it), I'll change it up a little bit. The amount of ingredients was about right. The cooking experience: I maintained the 2 qt liquid amount during the 3 hr simmering, also otherwise the soup would be lacking and end up with just moist meat & veggies, skimmed the debris every hour. Roasting the chx, in my oven for 40 minutes, the internal chx temp was 147 degrees, so I roasted it for another 15 minutes and it was perfect. The only thing I added to the soup was 1/2 a bunch of finely diced Italian parsley. Added it near the end of the soup process, & the pepper flakes. Had some garlic bread with the soup. All in all this is a keeper!

I made the roasted chicken broth from Costco roaster chicken legs. They package them for sale for $4.99 (approximately 2.75 lbs) and sell them in the prepared fresh food case. To make the stock, I separated the bones/skin from the meat and covered with water, reserving the meat for use in the dish later with extra left over. This made a wonderful rich broth.
Chef John is simply awesome and this chicken soup is as authentic and delicious as they come. Worth making the homemade roasted chicken broth.
I used frozen mixed vegetables and homemade bone broth. I added 1 bay leaf and few thin slices of ginger.

I did use a lovely lemon pepper Rotisserie chicken from the store... used all the meat I could harvest and double the veggies. (made the soup for my parents who had really bad colds and both like the veggies in the recipe). easy to follow, I did add a couple extras for some immune boosters (diced up mushrooms, a pinch of powdered ginger, tumeric and garlic...a teaspoonish of ACV and a fine diced sweet potato nuked in the microwave until soft). I know ... sorry... I don't feel these would change the overall outcome. Anyway, the soup was a success. I did make the noodles separate so my parents could reheat as needed and not have mushy pasta. now my mom is a great cook... and Dad commented he really liked that soup so I said thanks... then the odd look ... had to say I made it. I think this is day 5 and the soup is about gone and that is all he wants it seems for at least one meal. Mom had to buy more noodles. :-p once in a while we "kids" have a great win, so thanks Chef for this awesome recipe. I kept a bowl for myself and indeed... VERY VERY good.
Doubled the recipe and had five quarts to freeze for five more dinners. Making the roast chicken broth was a lot of work but worth it.

Update: round two. So, I did it again. This time doubling the veggies, using regular store bought chicken broth (not low sodium this time), added a heaping spoonful of minced garlic, and actually added the cayenne this time too. I also used 3/4 of a bag of No Yolk egg noodles. Oh, and I even seasoned the chicken while cooking it with Totes Cajun Seasoning. The husband/chef said it's way better now and is requesting I stick with my tweaks. Thank you for the inspiration! I will definitely be checking out your other recipes!!! My husband is a food snob chef, probably why he's a food snob. That being said, I'm a vegetarian looking for a healthy alternative to a Culinary classic to cook for my husband to eat while he's ill. I'm no chef, so I did the best I could. I don't have access to chicken fat. Nor did I make the broth from scratch. I used an organic pre-made low sodium chicken broth. The recipe was easy to follow. While I won't taste it he's on his second bowl as I write this review. He said it's bland and could use more noodles. Something I could definitely work with. When I make this again I'll be adding garlic, as well as more noodles. I'll maybe not use low sodium broth too. I definitely want to try making the broth from scratch when I have more time to put into it. This is saved to my favorites and I'll definitely be making it again.

Absolutely delicious! I think the Roasted Chicken Broth was the key, and worth every bit of the (actually quite small) effort! The only changes I made were doubling all the veges. I'll be making this again and again!!

Another winner from Chef John, and this time it's a lot easier and with fewer ingredients than most of his recipes. This chicken noodle soup is hearty and comforting. It takes some time to make if you also use his roasted chicken broth recipe, but that recipe provides you with the chicken, chicken fat, and broth called for in this recipe so it's worth the effort. Despite what he says in the video for this recipe about not overloading the soup, I used an entire 16oz bag of extra wide egg noodles because I like the pasta in my chicken noodle soup. Also he got it right calling for 5 minutes of cook time for the noodles, even tho the bag says 7-9 minutes. At 7-9 minutes the noodles would be too mushy.
Love this recipe as a stand alone but also as a base. So easy to add extras, such as broccoli and cauliflower. Never the same always delicious!

I tend not to change Chef John's recipes; but I do add peaches and cream corn kernels to add that extra flavor. I freeze individual portions. Sometimes I will add a little hot sauce to the individual portion for a little more kick than the cayenne.
